georgaello:study:1.title: Georgaello nom. nov., a replacement name for Aellopos Münster, 1836 (Chondrichthyes, Neoselachii) (Zootaxa, 2026)

facts.statement: Georgaello lived in the Late Jurassic period in what is now Germany.
Georgaello belongs to the class Chondrichthyes and infraclass Neoselachii.
The type species of Georgaello is Georgaello elongata, originally described by Münster in 1836.
Another species assigned to the genus is Georgaello wagneri, described by Agassiz in 1843.
Georgaello contains two species, G. elongata and G. wagneri, both found in Germany.
facts.quote: It contains two species, G. elongata and G. wagneri, which have been found in Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype specimens of both G. elongata and G. wagneri are housed at the Bayerische Staatssammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie.
facts.quote: The holotypes of both species are housed at the Bayerische Staatssammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie

facts.statement: Some vertebrae were later extracted from the G. elongata holotype and possibly transferred to the University of Wrocław.
facts.quote: some vertebrae were later extracted from the A. elongata holotype and possibly taken to the Uniwersytet Wrocławski

facts.statement: G. wagneri was the first chondrichthyan recognized from the Solnhofen Limestone.
facts.quote: G. wagneri was the first chondrichthyan recognized from the Solnhofen Limestone

facts.statement: G. elongata was one of the earliest named distinct genus and species of Jurassic sharks.
facts.quote: G. elongata was one of the first named as a distinct genus and species

facts.statement: The classification of Georgaello cannot be resolved beyond Neoselachii because the holotypes lack complete illustrations and their anatomy is uncertain.
facts.quote: Currently, the classification of Georgaello cannot be narrowed down past Neoselachii due to a lack of illustrations of the entire holotypes, uncertainty over which museum specimens the holotypes correspond to, and conflicting descriptions of the anatomy.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of G. elongata show a tectospondylic calcification pattern similar to that of Pseudorhina species and Notidanoides muensteri.
facts.quote: The figured vertebrae of G. elongata have a tectospondylic calcification pattern like those of Pseudorhina spp. and Notidanoides muensteri

facts.statement: Dermal denticles of Georgaello match morphotypes found in several other Jurassic sharks such as Asterodermus platypterus and Pseudorhina alifera.
facts.quote: The figured dermal denticles match morphotypes found in Asterodermus platypterus, Pseudorhina alifera, Phorcynis catulina, Palaeoscyllium formosum, Paracestracion falcifer, and Macrourogaleus hassei

rejected.statement: Georgaello is a valid genus of extinct neoselachian fish named by Greenfield in 2026.
Georgaello is a replacement name for the pre‑occupied genus Aellopos, which was first used by Münster in 1836.
rejected.quote: A replacement name for Aellopos Münster (1836)
